flake), add an explicit `wait_for` on this same selector with
`state: "visible"` before the click, rather than relying on the click
step's own built-in interactability check.

# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 This test case has been explicitly marked as failed.
⚠ ErrorThis test case has been explicitly marked as failed.
🖼️ Live Page Screenshot — the actual front-end element click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
Submitting a PARTIAL credit memo (qty 2 of 4) fails to save at all — the page redirects back to the same "New Credit Memo" form showing "The credit memo couldn't be saved.", and the DB confirms nothing persisted (sales_creditmemo has zero rows for this order, total_refunded stays NULL). A FULL credit memo (test 4, same store, same flow) saves correctly, so the bug is specific to partial-quantity refunds. Traced via SSH/DB to the exact mechanism: Magento's core Sales\Model\Order\Creditmemo\Save::execute() catches any \Exception from CreditmemoManagement::refund(), which in this store's stack dispatches the sales_order_creditmemo_save_after event to Webkul\Marketplace\Observer\SalesOrderCreditmemoSaveAfterObserver::execute() (app/code/Webkul/Marketplace/Observer/SalesOrderCreditmemoSaveAfterObserver.php) — a ~250-line seller-earning-split recalculation with no try/catch of its own, unlike this store's own Kemana\Marketplace\Plugin\VendorRefundEarningPlugin (an AFTER plugin on the same observer) which safely wraps everything in try/catch and logs instead of throwing. Whatever throws inside Webkul's observer propagates uncaught, gets wrapped by CreditmemoRepository::save() as CouldNotSaveException("The credit memo couldn't be saved."), rolls back the whole DB transaction, and is never written to exception.log (it's a LocalizedException subtype, which the controller's catch branch shows directly without logging — only the generic \Exception branch logs via $logger->critical()). The exact failing line inside Webkul's observer was not pinned down (couldn't attach a debugger over SSH); the file's per-seller commission/tax/qty math (lines ~180-330) is the prime suspect, since it assumes patterns that may not hold for a partial (non-full-order) refund quantity.
❌ Problematic Code
`app/code/Webkul/Marketplace/Observer/SalesOrderCreditmemoSaveAfterObserver.php`
— vendor/third-party code, not something to patch directly. The
specific failure point within its `execute()` method needs a debugger
or added logging to isolate precisely.
✅ Fixed Code
Not attempted — this is vendor code, and the precise failing line
needs isolating first (temporarily wrap the observer's body in
try/catch with full exception logging to identify it, then decide
whether to fix upstream or add a Kemana-side BEFORE plugin that
guards the specific bad input).
📋 What To Do
Report to devops/the dev team as a confirmed real defect: any partial (non-full-quantity) credit memo on this store currently fails to save, with no error detail surfaced beyond a generic message. This blocks real business use of partial refunds, not just this test. Recommend adding logging inside SalesOrderCreditmemoSaveAfterObserver::execute() (or wrapping it in a diagnostic try/catch) on a non-prod environment to capture the actual exception, since it is currently invisible in both exception.log and system.log.
